conventions.convention: A symmetry datum consists of C² maps (τ, ξ, B) on I₀ × Q satisfying the Noether identity on the entire state domain. Strict means τ = 0; time independence of ξ is an additional condition.
The generator acts by x ↦ x + sξ and t ↦ t + sτ. Its charge is C = (Mv)·ξ − (K + U)τ − B. Reversing the parameter negates the generator, boundary function and charge.
For parameter dimension σ, ξ has dimension length/σ, τ has dimension duration/σ, and B and C have dimension action/σ.

Translation directions are nonzero dimensionless vectors and the translation parameter has length units. Differential invariance is equivalent to finite invariance along admissible segments; separated interval components require agreement of their potential constants.
Rotations use ξᵢ = a × xᵢ, dimensionless a and a radian parameter. The charge is +a·J about the inertial origin. Finite invariance across excluded arcs requires component compatibility.

The boost parameter has velocity units, ξᵢ = ta, B = a·Σmᵢxᵢ, and Kₐ = a·(tP − MX) has mass-length units. An admissible boosted curve is a motion exactly when the potential gradients at paired endpoints agree.

For a C³ moving coordinate map X with invertible Xq, the sign of the energy correction is E_in = e + ⟨Xt, Mx′⟩. Conservation of e requires the chart Euler–Lagrange equation and vanishing explicit chart-Lagrangian time derivative along the curve.

load_bearing.statement: A symmetry datum is a C² triple (τ, ξ, B) satisfying Ltτ + Lx·ξ + Lv·(Dtξ − vDtτ) + LDtτ = DtB on O; its charge is C = (Mv)·ξ − (K + U)τ − B.

For a symmetry datum, C is constant along every motion when d ≡ 0. For an arbitrary presentation, C′ = ⟨d, ξ − x′τ⟩, and C is constant exactly when this pairing vanishes throughout the motion. Replacing U by U + c(t) and B by B − cτ, with c of class C², preserves the identity and charge.

For a strict datum with time-independent ξ and d ≡ 0, its charge is constant along every motion. For any strict datum and arbitrary presentation, C′ = ⟨d, ξ⟩, with conservation exactly when this pairing vanishes throughout the motion.

The condition Σa·∇ᵢU = 0 everywhere is equivalent to invariance along every simultaneous translation segment contained in Q. It gives the strict translation datum and, when d ≡ 0, conservation of a·P. A nonzero directional derivative at a state produces a maximal motion with nonzero momentum-component derivative there.

The datum (τ, ξ, B) = (1, 0, 0) satisfies the identity exactly when ∂tU ≡ 0. With d ≡ 0 this gives conservation of K + U; if ∂tU(t₀, x₀) ≠ 0, the maximal motion through (t₀, x₀, 0) has that nonzero energy derivative at t₀.

For every stated C² chart curve, E_in = e + ⟨Xt, Mx′⟩. If the curve solves the chart Euler–Lagrange equation and the explicit chart-Lagrangian time derivative vanishes along it, e is constant. For d ≡ 0, chart descriptions of model motions solve that equation.

concerns.concern: The physical_scope states that under differential translation invariance in the global potential branch 'the boosted curves t -> x(t) + s t a of motions are again motions'. This omits the endpoint-gradient condition correctly present in Statement clause 4 and is false even when the boosted curve stays admissible. In numerical SI coordinates take N = 1, m = 1, a = e₁, I₀ = J = (0.9, 1.1), Q = ((−1,1) × R²) ∪ ((2,4) × R²), and the smooth potential U = 0 on the first slab and U = x₂ on the second, with d = 0. The differential translation condition holds everywhere. The stationary curve x(t) = 0 is a motion; with s = 3 its admissible boost is (3t,0,0), whose acceleration is zero but whose force is −e₂, so it is not a motion. The public scope must carry the qualifications already proved in clause 4.

seams_checked.note: Uses L = K − U, the d = 0 Newton/Euler–Lagrange equivalence and C³ full-dimensional coordinate covariance with invertible Xq. Residual-force motions are handled by direct differentiation rather than falsely asserting stationarity.

Strict time-independent generators match the chart point-symmetry definition. The general identity and charge match the mathematical Noether theorem; moving-chart energy uses local product restrictions to meet the hyperregular chart hypotheses.
Preserves the declared potential representative and residual split, the definitions of P, X and J, and E′ = ∂tU + ⟨d,x′⟩.
Retains continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz force maps and C² motions. Sharpness uses a unique maximal motion through an admissible datum on an open interval containing its initial time.
Uses fixed positive masses, one inertial coordinate frame, open configuration domains and the SI dimension conventions; Galilean frame availability is kept distinct from potential symmetry.
The uniform-force curve is the supplier's explicit maximal motion. Other example force maps satisfy the standing regularity and their proposed curves are checked directly against Newton's equation.
Uses the same potential, momentum, centre-of-mass and angular-momentum definitions and the zero-residual energy rate. Numerical values are explicitly model parameters and predictions.
The rotating example uses the stated substitution x′ = Xt + Xqv and the transport identity with d = 0 and invertible rotation matrix.
Parameter units and charge dimensions agree with the framework conventions; all masses are positive and every model's configuration domain is stated.
The rotating Lagrangian has C² mechanical coefficients and positive-definite G = mI, so the cited hyperregularity and Hamiltonian formulas apply.
The displayed rotating matrix satisfies RᵀR = I and det R = 1, matching the SO(3) definition and inverse-transpose lemma.
